name: Big Chalk Nature Recovery Fund

funder.name: Big Chalk partnership (Protected Landscapes Partnership, supported by Defra)

summary: Capital grants to create, restore and connect habitats such as species-rich grassland, ancient woodland and chalk streams on chalk and limestone landscapes across southern England, assessed on a rolling basis.

steps: Discuss the proposal with a fund manager, if invited

eligibility.rule: Be a legitimate organisation with appropriate governance arrangements
Have a UK bank account in the applicant's name
Work in the Big Chalk area or on chalk or limestone streams or rivers originating in or closely linked to it.
Hold appropriate insurance for the activities undertaken
Own the land, have at least five years left on the tenancy, or have clear written landowner permission.
Ensure the land can be managed for conservation until 2032
Complete Year 1 capital works by 31 March 2027 unless agreed otherwise
Have or be able to access the skills, knowledge and capacity to deliver the project.

calls.label: Rolling applications

status.quote: Organisations and individuals working to restore nature in southern England can apply now for grants of up to £100,000

opens.quote: Submit your Expression of Interest 25 September 2026

calls.note: Projects would normally need to be completed by 31 March 2027.

applicant_types.quote: We welcome applications from environmental charities, farmers, land managers and landowners, community groups, local authorities, parish and town councils, educational institutions that manage land, and collaborative partnerships working within chalk and limestone landscapes.

geography.quote: The fund supports nature recovery projects across southern England on chalk and limestone geology

access.quote: Submit an Expression of Interest - tell us about your project, what you want to achieve and how it will benefit nature.

amount.quote: Capital grants from £1,000 to £100,000, with larger awards available exceptionally

co_finance_required.quote: The fund can contribute up to 80% of project costs (exceptionally up to 100%)

consortium_required.quote: Projects can be delivered by individual organisations or through collaboration between partners.

effort.quote: After reading this guidance, please submit an expression of interest.
Initial eligibility check (typically within 2 to 5 working days).
You will then be invited to complete the online application form and submit the required supporting documents.
Full assessment, with timescales depending on the size and complexity of the grant requested.
If eligible, you will be invited to discuss your proposal with a Fund Manager.

eligibility.quote: Be a legitimate organisation, business, charity, public body or community group with appropriate governance arrangements in place.
Have a UK bank account in the name of the organisation or business applying for the grant.

Deliver a project within the Big Chalk Programme Area. Projects relating to chalk or limestone streams and rivers that originate within, or are closely connected to, the programme area may also be considered.
Hold appropriate insurance cover for the activities being undertaken.
Own the land, hold a tenancy for at least a further 5 years, or have clear written permission from the landowner to carry out the proposed work.
Be able to demonstrate that the land can continue to be managed for the intended conservation outcomes until at least 2032.
Be able to complete any Year 1 capital works by 31 March 2027 (unless otherwise agreed for ecological or operational reasons).
Have, or be able to access, the skills, knowledge and capacity needed to successfully deliver the project.

after_award.quote: Small grants (£1,000 to £10,000): A short completion report and photographs demonstrating delivery of the project. Standard grants (£10,000 to £100,000): Quarterly progress reports during delivery
